text: The names this story designs are accepted for the rwb-asset quality model: tables asset_quality_run, asset_quality_result and asset_quality_break in rwb_asset; one rec code REC-05 with the check names COUNT, VALUE and KEY, since the FSD P1 defines REC-05 as the resolution of every business key compared on business key, count and amount; the run states Not run, Running, Released, Held and Failed with the result values PASS and BREAK; the workflow AssetQualityWorkflow with four activities; the read operations GET /quality-runs/{businessDate}, GET /quality-results and GET /assets on the base /api/recovery/asset/v1; and the migration V1011_1__asset_quality.sql. The Schedule cron and the column of the asset row that holds the ACE asset key are Not specified in the source documents (CG-B2-S5-026-1; ASM-B2-S5-026-6).
why: TSD S5 declares asset, listing and asset_sale only, names no column holding the ACE asset key, and carries no quality, run, break or report object; the run still has to be buildable and testable without inventing a business value, so the design names only structures, and every value it carries is a parameter or reference data.

text: The run keeps the legacy business-date cadence and runs every business date, while DP06 Collateral and assets refreshes WEEKLY at MON 08:00 in the data product catalog. The completeness gate therefore reads the DP06 freshness answer for the business date in force: an answer that is LOADED lets the checks run against those rows, and an answer that is STALE or names an earlier load date holds the date with that date as the reason, exactly as the legacy X3 path holds JOB-04.
why: The legacy story runs every business date and the FSD S5 precondition accepts a data product that shows its date as stale, while FSD P1 A2.2 gives DP06 a weekly refresh; the two cadences cannot both be met without a gate, and a gate is what the legacy story already applies to a missing ACE batch.
